'''Fire arrow''' is an early game [[:Category:Arrows|arrow]]. It is useful against several enemies in both the [[Meadows]] and the [[Black Forest]] biomes which fear or are weak to fire. 

== Availability ==

* Crafted at a [[Workbench]]
* Found in chests in [[Abandoned House]]s, buried in [[Viking Graveyard]] and inside [[Burial Chambers]]

== Features ==

* Deals both [[fire]] and [[pierce]] damage, applying the [[burning]] DOT effect.
* [[Wet Effect|Wet]] enemies (indicated by dripping water) will extinguish the burning quickly, causing very little damage.
* Provides ambient lighting when fired on dry surfaces.
* When fired on surfaces that are underwater, fire arrows will be extinguished and will not provide any ambient lighting. However, if fired onto an initially dry surface, and it goes underwater (e.g. waves rolling in on shorelines), fire arrows will remain lit.

'''Ooze bomb''' is a thrown weapon that creates a [[Poison]] 4-meter radius AoE cloud, which stays for 10 seconds. Anyone in the cloud (excluding the thrower) takes 40 poison damage over 7 seconds. If an enemy stays in the cloud, the damage is refreshed, so the maximum damage is 40*(10+7)/7 = 97.

Damage value does not depend on any player skill, but may be altered by enemy resistance.

== Availability ==
* Crafted with the [[Workbench]], stacks up to 50
* [[Ooze]] can be found in the [[Swamp]] biome by killing [[Blob]]s and [[Oozer]]s
* [[Leather Scraps]] are found in [[Chest]]s in the [[Meadows]] biome, dropped from [[Boar]]s or [[Bat]]s or mined from [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s.
* [[Resin]] is dropped by [[Greydwarf]], [[Greydwarf Shaman]] and [[Greydwarf Brute]]. It has a chance of dropping from chopped [[Birch]] and [[Pine]] trees, and [[Beech|Smaller Beech Trees]].

Bow (4 seconds) | veryweak = | weak = Blunt, Fire | resistant = Pierce, Frost | veryresistant = | immune = Poison | stagger = 50%}} }} The '''Dead Raiser''' is one of the four [[Mistlands]] [[Magic]] weapons. When cast, a '''Skelett''' (a tamed [[Skeleton]]) spawns near the caster. The skelett will follow its summoner and attacks any non-tame creature that comes close, except for neutral [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. They are much stronger than normal Skeletons, even compared to [[Creature Level|2-star]] variants. In addition to requiring up to 100 [[Eitr]] to be cast, the caster will lose up to 40% of their current [[Health]] (''not'' their maximum health). Like the other magic weapons, it has no secondary ability. Similarly, how much health is drained upon casting is also affected by the caster's [[Blood magic]] level, as is how much eitr is required: at level 100, both will be reduced by 1/3. ==Skelett== '''Skeletts''' are [[Creatures]] summoned by players using the [[Dead Raiser]]. As summons, they fight on behalf of nearby players, attacking any nearby hostile creatures. Otherwise, they look and behave similar to [[Skeleton]]s, except for being purple in color. Skeletts come in two variants: A melee-oriented type with sword and (optionally) shield, and an archer type with a bow and arrows. The amount of damage dealt by its summons is highly dependent on the caster's [[Blood magic]] skill level: each Skelett's damage increases by 2% per level up to a maximum of +200% (x3) of their base values (at level 100). Their [[Health]] is not affected by skill level. Summoned skeletts will randomly spawn with a [[Bronze Sword]] (80% chance) or a wooden [[Bows|bow]] (20% chance); if the skelett has a sword, it may also spawn with a [[Wood Shield]] or a [[Bronze Buckler]] (25% chance each). Depending on the location, it may be advantageous to re-summon for melee- or archery-specific Skeletons. The Dead Raiser has a limit to how many summons it can control at once, which depends on its quality; if a player casts the Dead Raiser when they already have summoned the maximum number of skeletts, their oldest skelett will be killed off and a new one will be summoned. == Upgrade information == {| class="wikitable" !Quality !1 !2 !3 !4 |- !Maximum Skeletons Controllable |1 |2 |3 |4 |- !Durability |200 |250 |300 |350 |- !Crafting |10 [[Bone Fragments]]

It is very dim compared to most proper light sources, but can provide a small amount of light in the dark. ** The glow effect also makes players slightly easier to detect while [[Sneak_(Skill)|sneaking]], increasing the visibility of its holder by approximately 10%. * As of the Mistlands update, no single [[Food]] item grants sufficient Eitr for players with low skill at Blood magic to use the Dead Raiser: Such players must consume at least two Eitr-focused foods to use it, leaving them with a lower maximum potential health pool. ** [[Blood magic]] level 47 is currently the minimum skill level at which a single food item ([[Seeker Aspic]]) will allow a player to cast the Dead Raiser. ** The high eitr requirement can be mitigated somewhat: Casters only need sufficient Eitr at the time of casting, not afterward. Therefore, players are somewhat free to eat different foods (either after waiting or through use of [[Bukeperries]]) after using the Dead Raiser, especially if they plan on keeping their Skeletts protected through use of e.g. the [[Staff of Protection]]. However, should one of their Skeletts die, they will become unable to summon any more until they once again have the required amount of eitr. * As of the Ashlands update, the best [[Food]] item for Eitr is [[Marinated Greens]], which still does not provide enough Eitr alone to use Dead Raiser until players have raised their [[Blood magic]] somewhat. ** Players who wish to use Dead Raiser with low Blood Magic can pair one Eitr food with [[Ashlands Gourmet Bowl]] or [[Mushrooms Galore á la Mistlands]] to somewhat mitigate the loss of health or stamina inherent to pairing two Eitr-specific foods. * Skeletts cannot swim or drown, and will instead walk on the seafloor. * Skeletts are considered ''tameable'' mobs, but are also ''always'' tame. This means that they can be pet like other tameable mobs. Additionally, like all tamed mobs, players are only able to ''damage'' them either by using the [[Butcher Knife]] or by enabling friendly fire mode. If the [[Dead Raiser]] is used by the player after the maximum number of Skeletts have been summoned, the oldest Skelett will be ''killed'' off and replaced with a new one. ** Killing a summoned Skelett before exceeding the maximum frees up one of the summoner's summon slots. They can then use the Dead Raiser to re-summon a new Skelett. This can be done on purpose to obtain the desired Skelett variants, or just to quickly get new ones with full health. * Skeletts are able to be shielded with a [[Staff of Protection]] in the same way that players can be. ==List of names== Skeletts always spawn with one of 99 possible names. They can also be re-named by players.
